questions.stem: A block of mass $m = 10\ \mathrm{kg}$ is resting on a rough inclined plane of inclination $30^\circ$. The coefficient of friction is $\mu = 0.5$. What is the minimum force $F$ applied parallel to the inclined plane to keep the block from sliding down? (Take $g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$)
questions.solution:
The component of gravity down the incline is $mg\sin\theta = 10 \times 10 \times \sin 30^\circ = 50\ \mathrm{N}$.
The limiting friction force is $f_{\text{max}} = \mu mg\cos\theta = 0.5 \times 10 \times 10 \times \cos 30^\circ = 25\sqrt{3} \approx 43.3\ \mathrm{N}$.
To prevent sliding down, the force $F$ must satisfy $F + f_{\text{max}} \ge mg\sin\theta$.
$F_{\text{min}} = mg\sin\theta - f_{\text{max}} = 50 - 43.3 = 6.7\ \mathrm{N}$.

questions.stem: A block of mass $M$ slides down on a rough inclined plane of inclination $\theta$ with constant velocity. If this block is projected up the same inclined plane with an initial velocity $v_0$, the distance up to which the block will rise on the incline before coming to rest is:
questions.solution:
Since the block slides down with constant velocity, the downward force of gravity equals friction: $Mg \sin\theta = f_k = \mu_k Mg \cos\theta \implies \mu_k = \tan\theta$.
When projected up, the retardation is $a = g \sin\theta + \mu_k g \cos\theta = g \sin\theta + (\tan\theta) g \cos\theta = 2g \sin\theta$.
Using $v^2 - u^2 = 2as \implies 0 - v_0^2 = -2(2g \sin\theta)s \implies s = \frac{v_0^2}{4g \sin\theta}$.

questions.stem: A block of mass $5\ \mathrm{kg}$ is placed on a rough horizontal surface. The coefficient of static friction between the block and the surface is $0.6$ and the coefficient of kinetic friction is $0.4$. A horizontal force of $25\ \mathrm{N}$ is applied to the block. The frictional force acting on the block is ______ $\mathrm{N}$. (Take $g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$)
questions.solution:
Maximum static frictional force $f_{s,\text{max}} = \mu_s N = \mu_s m g = 0.6 \times 5 \times 10 = 30\ \mathrm{N}$.
Since the applied force $F = 25\ \mathrm{N}$ is less than $f_{s,\text{max}} = 30\ \mathrm{N}$, the block remains at rest.
Therefore, static friction adjusts to balance the applied force: $f = F = 25\ \mathrm{N}$.
